tools.name: list_peers
tools.description: [agent-messenger v0.7.0] List other Claude Code sessions connected to the broker (id, name, hostname, cwd, repo, summary).

scope.description: "all" = every host (default). "host" = same hostname. "directory" = same cwd. "repo" = same git repository.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: [agent-messenger v0.7.0] Send a message to another Claude Code session by peer name or id (from list_peers). Works across hosts.

delivery.description: "pull" (default) = the receiver sees only an unread notice (sender shown) and reads the text with check_messages. "push" = the text is shown in the receiver's conversation directly.

tools.name: send_ping
tools.description: [agent-messenger v0.7.0] Send a liveness signal to a peer, optionally with a one-line subject (e.g. the task id or name being worked on). The receiver sees a one-line ping notice (sender and subject shown), nothing to read or reply to. Use it periodically during long work so the orchestrator can tell progress from a stall.

subject.description: Optional one-line subject, e.g. the task id or name being worked on. Delivered as the message text.

tools.name: set_name
tools.description: [agent-messenger v0.7.0] Set a stable name for this session so other peers can address it by name.

tools.name: set_summary
tools.description: [agent-messenger v0.7.0] Set a 1-2 sentence summary of what this session is working on (visible in list_peers).

tools.name: check_messages
tools.description: [agent-messenger v0.7.0] Read and acknowledge unread messages from other sessions (the text behind an unread notice). Safe to call any time.

instructions:
agent-messenger v0.7.0

You are connected to agent-messenger. Other Claude Code sessions on this machine AND on remote hosts can find you and send you messages.

Inbound traffic arrives in the conversation as one of:
- "[agent-messenger] 未読 N 件（from <name>@<host>）…" — an unread notice. Call check_messages to read the text, reply with send_message if needed, then resume your work.
- "[agent-messenger] ping（from <name>@<host>）" or "…）: <subject>" — the sender is alive and working (subject = what it is working on, if given). Nothing to read, no reply needed.
- "[agent-messenger] message from <name>@<host>" followed by the text — sent with delivery "push". Reply with send_message if needed, then resume your work.

Tools:
- list_peers: discover sessions (scope: all / host / directory / repo)
- send_message: send to a peer by name or id (cross-host). delivery "pull" (default) = the receiver sees only an unread notice; "push" = the text is shown directly
- send_ping: send a liveness signal, optionally with a one-line subject such as the task id (e.g. periodically while working, so the orchestrator can tell progress from a stall)
- set_name: give this session a stable name (e.g. "master-cap", "agent-messenger") so others can address it by name
- set_summary: describe what you are working on (visible in list_peers)
- check_messages: read unread message texts. Notices are delivered into the conversation automatically (via the session inbox socket, or via channel push when Claude Code was started with --dangerously-load-development-channels server:agent-messenger); call check_messages any time to read.

On start, call set_name (if not already named) and set_summary.
